description: The one-pass plan a director emits after measuring, before cutting. Times are seconds unless a field says otherwise.

duckDb.description: Absolute music level under speech in dB; a negative target attenuates from unity. Convert through clip_audio_levels_db; never pass this number directly as the engine's linear volume.

mood.description: Mood words the bed shops by when no query is given (bgm_search reads mood: 'epic tension', 'chillhop', 'upbeat').

glossary.description: The recogniser's glossary - proper nouns, acronyms and jargon the take uses, handed to Whisper as its initial prompt so the spelling the opening words establish is the one the whole run keeps. At most 200 characters; absent is Whisper's own cold start.

language.description: The take's language as an ISO code or BCP-47 tag (bn, bn-BD, en, hi). When absent, the runner reads the plan's own script and otherwise lets whisper detect the language. A non-English language never runs on an English-only (.en) model.

source.description: tts = tts_generate made it; file = user-provided.

speed.description: Playback rate for the generated take; 1.0 is natural.

voice.description: TTS voice id (Kokoro 0-52; e.g. 2 af_bella, 8 af_river, 11 am_adam).

whisperModel.description: The recogniser's model for this take (e.g. base, small, base.en). The multilingual default applies when absent; an English-only model named against a non-English language is replaced by its multilingual counterpart.

audioClipId.description: Optional real timeline clip id for the already-placed voiceover. The runner reuses this clip but does not cut it; plan segment times must already match the clip. Never invent the id.

captions.description: Video-wide caption style; the current transcription/caption pipeline provides segment timing, not word alignment. Per-segment flags override presence only.

background.description: Optional plate '#rrggbb[aa]' for readability; null = no plate.

fontSize.description: Fraction of frame height; 0.04 engine default, 0.05-0.06 for short-form.

offsetY.description: Fraction from center; positive is lower.

syncMode.description: Only segment-level timing is supported; do not claim word-level synchronization.

creativeBrief.description: The WHY of the piece. A plan without this is structurally valid but creatively unready: plan_validate reports creativeReady=false and lists blockers. Set it with creative_brief before planning.

audience.description: Who this is for, specifically enough to choose shots for. Not 'everyone' - name the person, their problem and what they already believe.

avoid.description: Clichés and stock shots to refuse (e.g. generic handshake, lens flare, waving flag).

brandKit.description: Colours, fonts, logo/end-card rules. Object or a short string.

constraints.description: Hard limits: runtime, footage you must use, claims you cannot make.

curiosityGap.description: The question opened in the first 1-2 seconds. It must be answerable by the payoff.

emotionalArc.description: Three or more emotional beats in order. Either an array of strings (e.g. ['unease','wonder','relief']) or one string separated by '->' or commas.

goal.description: What the viewer should think, feel or do after the last frame.

monetized.description: True when the edit ships on a monetised channel or as client work. Arms the licence gates: plan_validate blocks OpenVid B-roll and MobyGratis beds, openvid_import refuses outright (the index carries no per-clip licence record), and bgm_import refuses MobyGratis (non-commercial only). Default false.

payoff.description: What resolves the curiosityGap. If this is weak, no amount of motion will save the edit.

platform.description: Where it plays (tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube, ...). Determines hook length, safe margins and pacing.

referenceStyle.description: A director/editor/show whose rhythm and taste this cut borrows from, and what exactly to borrow.

signalEvidence.description: The run's own reading of every voice_signals family, with the confidence the profile gave each: {measured: [family...], leanOn: ['family 0.92'...], leanLessOn: [...], whyWeak: {family: basis}}. Present only when the run measured a profile; a family at confidence 0 is left out rather than offered.

thesis.description: The one sentence the whole video argues or reveals. Every shot serves it.

tone.description: Voice and attitude: e.g. dry, urgent, awed, conspiratorial.

platform.description: youtube, shorts, reels, tiktok — sets loudness/length expectations only.

grade.description: Required. A video with no grade is a rough cut.

apply.description: layer = ONE effect_layer_add {start: 0, duration: <runtime>} with duration WRITTEN (absent defaults to 5 s - the trap); perClip = the same videoEffects chain on every clip.

filter.description: One of the 57 filter ids, e.g. concat.teal-orange, concat.noir, concat.warm.

intensity.description: Value within the param's min/max from effects_list.

intensityKey.description: The package's own intensity param key from effects_list (concat.teal-orange -> 'amount' 0-100; concat.warm/cool -> 'temperature' in K).

maxSegmentSeconds.description: Hard floor P: no visual segment runs past this (4.0 energetic niches, 6.0 calm).

mode.description: reel = retention engineering (<= 60 s, hook in 3 s, loop or single CTA, interrupts every 2-4 s); longform = an argument with chapters (> 60 s, hook -> title -> chapters -> re-hook at the 50-60% dip -> outro CTA). See prompts/reels_vs_longform.md.

niche.description: The niche playbook in use, e.g. history, tech, luxury, motivation, finance, science, horror, fitness, gaming, howto.

retention.description: The retention contract: what earns the first three seconds, where the turn lands, what pays it off, and the pattern breaks that keep a scroll from becoming a swipe. A plan without it is not creativeReady.

hook.description: What the first three seconds show or say, and the open question it plants.

openLoops.description: The questions the viewer needs answered; at least two, one answered by the payoff.

patternBreaks.description: Times where the visual or sonic pattern deliberately changes (a new shot size, a silence, a colour turn, a camera move). At least two.

payoffAt.description: The second the promise is answered; normally the last 10-20% of the cut.

turnAt.description: The second the argument or feeling turns; normally 40-60% of the cut.

sections.description: The piece's structure, by role. Reel: hook + curiosity + progression + payoff + ending. Longform: hook + intro + curiosity + progression + rehook + payoff + cta + ending. Boundaries align to segments.

segments.description: The timeline, in order. Segment i covers [start, end); gaps or overlaps are plan errors.

act.description: The dramaturgical act this segment plays - the emotion read assigns it, the plan's sections may override it. Drives the shot register (extreme close-up for a hook, wide establishing for setup, hero shot for the reveal) and the BGM duck depth.

captions.description: Whether captions are included for this segment; timing is segment-level, not word-aligned. Null = follow the video default.

colourTemp.description: The colour-temperature push this segment rides on top of the base grade, from the emotion read (fear is cold and crushed, joy golden and lifted, disgust sickly).

comp.description: The designed beat on this segment (motion_bake / captions_animate). Density floor: one per section, one per 15 s.

hold.description: Seconds the comp holds on screen.

ops.description: Authoring operations: set-slot, set-text, set-words, retime, pop, fade-in, ...

cutType.description: How this segment begins; the eighteen-cut vocabulary in prompts/cuts_and_pacing.md. A run of six hards is a pacing smell.

duckDb.description: How deep the BGM ducks under this segment's speech, as an absolute dB target from the act's profile in the emotion read (-15 under the naked hook, -9 letting the reveal ride).

easing.description: How this segment's motion enters, from the emotion: tense lines ease in, warm ones ease out, a burst pops, anger snaps.

oneOf.description: The exact concat-motion authoring curve object the emotion read returns ({kind: bezier|spring, ...}).

emotion.description: What this segment's narration FEELS like, from the `emotion` tool's read of the transcript (action extract). The layer every other per-segment choice answers to: the easing, the colour push, the SFX register, the stock vocabulary.

in.description: The entrance; hard floor M: every clip enters on purpose.

anim.description: static = deliberate, at most one per piece.

musicArrangement.description: The bed as structure, not one flat track: sections with reasons, timed to the story, each change landed on a cutSafePoint or a downbeat.

licence.description: FreePD is CC0; Lo-Fi is MobyGratis non-commercial; a TinyMusician bed never ships monetized.

sections.description: The arrangement's sections, in time order.

automation.description: The duck keyframes and section dips the mix rides (the duckDb floor under speech, the lift in pauses, the dip before a reveal).

reason.description: Why the bed changes here - the chapter turn, the reveal, the outro.

structure.description: The track's own section (analyze_music_structure): intro, build, drop, outro.

source.description: The track id or file the arrangement is cut from (freepd id, or a generated file's path).

out.description: The exit or hand-off; section boundaries exit, interiors hand off.

gainDb.description: An absolute dB target; 0 dB is unity, negative levels attenuate, and -60 dB is the editor's silence floor. Typical SFX support levels are around -12 to -6 dB.

peakAt.description: The time the sound's PEAK must land on — usually the segment's first frame.

query.description: sounds_search query using a real category: Whoosh, Impact, Riser, Motion, UI, Notification, Keyboard, Digital, Foley, Writing, Ambience, Music.

soundEvents.description: One per placed accent: the sound decisions this segment executes, each landing its measured peak on a measured target. Cite the evidence in signalLog; a generated asset carries its prompt, seed, model kind and licence.

assetId.description: The shelf sound's id or the generated file's path.

confidence.description: The evidence quality behind the placement.

eventId.description: Unique within the plan; the receipts and the critic name the event by it.

gainDb.description: The starting level; keyframes ride it.

kind.description: Generated assets only: which generator wrote it.

licence.description: Generated assets only: the licence the reply carried - a monetized edit must be able to answer for it.

modelEvidence.description: The sense_sound_model record behind the choice (its id or hash), cited not copied.

peakAt.description: The MEASURED time the sound's own peak falls (sound_sense), not the manifest's syncAt.

prompt.description: Generated assets only: the words it was written from.

reason.description: One sentence: why this sound, here, for this beat.

role.description: The six-role vocabulary of prompts/sfx_design.md (impact, whoosh, riser, reveal, ambience, texture, or the shelf's own category word).

seed.description: Generated assets only: the seed that reproduces it.

source.description: Where the asset came from; a generator row records its birth.

start.description: Timeline start; computed as target minus the asset's measured peakAt.

storyBeat.description: The story moment the accent serves - an emphasis word, a cut, a reveal.

visualEvidence.description: The visual reading it synchronises with (the cut, the motion peak, the reveal).

voiceEvidence.description: The voice reading that timed it (the emphasis word, the pause class).

spoken.description: The narration words this segment covers (for caption grouping); for broll, a 40+ character fallback when visual.description is omitted or empty.

effect.description: One of the 122 transition ids, e.g. concat.dissolve, concat.whip-pan, concat.glitch-transition, concat.punch-in.

category.description: A concise semantic continuity category for this shot, such as people, landscape, machinery, or data.

clipId.description: A real OpenVid clip id or existing timeline clip id, returned by a tool; never invented.

description.description: For broll, a provided non-empty value must be at least 40 characters; if omitted or empty, segment.spoken must supply at least 40 characters; a short non-empty visual description takes precedence and is refused.

file.description: For a source file not yet represented by a clip or media id: its actual path.

fit.description: fill = clip_frame framing 'fill' (cover + crop; the default on every aspect mismatch - OpenVid is landscape-only, so 9:16 canvases fill from landscape sources). blurPlate = timeline_background blur as a deliberate style. A letterboxed frame at review is a defect.

hero.description: Whether this is the hero shot; widens candidate search.

mediaId.description: For existing footage: the media-bin id returned by project_get/timeline_read.

motionMin.description: Minimum measured motion score accepted for this shot.

preset.description: textCard/titleCard: one of the 31 text presets, e.g. concat.impact, concat.lower-third, concat.bold-caption.

queries.description: Fallback BM25 search phrases for this B-roll segment.

query.description: Required and non-empty for every broll segment: the primary OpenVid search query. Follow prompts/broll_matching.md.

shotScale.description: The intended shot scale, used by the continuity check.

storyboard.description: Required for textCard/titleCard segments and must contain at least one scene. Use the same storyboard schema as the motion_reel MCP tool; the rendered reel is imported and placed at this segment's start.

trimIn.description: Seconds into the source where the clip starts.

trimOut.description: Seconds into the source where it ends (leave longer than the segment; trim after placing).

type.description: broll = OpenVid clip; textCard/titleCard = styled text over background (fallbacks); existing = footage already imported.

signalLog.description: The decision log: which voice_signals signals drove each choice. One entry per cut, caption, graphic, BGM, transition, repair, mix, grade, SFX and motion decision, naming the signals (from the profile's decisionPolicy) behind it, with their confidence and a one-sentence basis. A `cut` entry must land on a segment boundary; an entry at an arbitrary time is not evidence that a cut was driven. A plan with a voiceover and no signalLog is NOT creativeReady.

at.description: Seconds into the timeline where the decision lands.

confidence.description: How certain the profile was of the signals behind this choice, 0-1: the weakest family it names. Required by the signal gate; an entry without it, or with 0, is refused.

decision.description: The kind of choice: where to cut, what a caption highlights, what graphic to add, whether to add BGM, where to transition, how the pacing moves, what the repair removes, how the mix is set, which grade the read chose, where the accents land, and how the motion is sized.

note.description: One sentence a reviewer reads: why these signals drove this choice. Required by the signal gate.

signals.description: The profile signals behind the choice, e.g. ["pause.class=dead_air", "emphasisWords", "speechRate.pace"].

slots.description:
The footage slots the edit spends: one opening at a time, with the
role it plays, the treatment that fills it, and the rich description
a stock search ranks against. Optional - a plan without slots is a
plan the segments alone describe. The b-roll slots must match the
b-roll segments one for one, and a segment that names its slot by
slotId must find it.

items.description:
One opening the edit promises a picture for.

The `description` is the contract with the search: a rich
noun-plus-adjective string of twelve to twenty-five words that CLIP
ranks the candidates against. The `queries` are the fallback keyword
phrases only - what BM25 gets when the description's shortlist comes
back thin. A treatment the edit draws itself takes no queries at all.

description.description:
The rich noun+adjective string the stock search ranks against,
twelve to twenty-five words: what is in frame, what it is doing,
what it feels like. The validator refuses anything under 40
characters - it is what CLIP ranks against.

durationS.description: How long the slot's screen time runs, in seconds.

entry.description: When the picture enters, against the words and the beat grid.

oneOf.description: On the emphasis the words carry.
Just before the line starts, so the picture is there to meet it.
On a beat the grid names.
After the line has landed - the picture follows the words.

Before the next emphasis the words carry, so the picture leaves
before it outstays its welcome.
On a beat the grid names.
Where the source clip itself cuts - the join hides in the source.

Early, before the words are done with it: the picture owes the
edit less than the span asks.

hero.description:
Whether this slot is the shot the thumbnail and the first glance
live on; a hero slot searches wider and ranks longer.

job.description: The work the slot's picture does for the edit.

oneOf.description: Show what the words describe.
Show the opposite the words sit against.
Land a beat - the punctuation mark the cut makes.
Bridge two stretches the edit joins.
Give the viewer a breath.

motionMin.description:
The least motion the slot's clip may carry, on the library's own
motion scale: a `breathe` slot wants stillness, a `punctuate`
slot wants the opposite.

queries.description:
The fallback keyword phrases only, for the BM25 pass. A treatment
the edit draws itself (hold, graphic, black) takes none; broll
takes at least one.

role.description:
The dramaturgical role the slot plays - the same seven acts a
segment's `act` names, because a slot spends a beat.

oneOf.description: The opening grab: read at a glance, over in a breath.
The ground the video stands on.
The problem, wound up.
The shift the video exists for.
The answer, shown.
The receipts.
The ask.

slotId.description:
The slot's own id, unique in the plan: `"hook.1"`, `"reveal.hero"`.
The per-slot notes the critic sends back name it.

oneOf.description: The A-roll holds: the picture stays where it is.
Stock footage covers the span.
The edit draws the span itself - a chart, a card, a caption.
Black, on purpose - the dip, the breath, the act break.

visualRationale.description:
A concise, film-specific reason for this visual choice. Required
in practice for major beats; it must explain intent rather than
repeat a template.

fallback.description:
A meaningful alternative if the selected asset, model, or renderer
is unavailable.

job.description: What this beat must communicate or make the viewer feel.

oneOf.description: Stock or imported footage.
A motion comp.
A chart.
Type on screen.
Generated imagery.
The A-roll holds.
More than one medium together.

reason.description:
Why this medium is stronger than the plausible alternatives for
this beat.

style.description:
The film-specific visual treatment: composition, palette, type,
movement, texture, or camera language.

transition.description:
Why and how the visual enters or leaves in relation to story,
speech, and rhythm.

style.description: The style bible: the one look the whole film wears. Set it before the plan; every segment, caption, comp, grade and sound choice must conform. A plan without it is structurally valid but not creativeReady, because five good shots in five different styles read as five videos.

captions.description: The one caption system: family, weight, case, accent colour and placement. Per-segment captions may change presence, never the system.

font.description: The caption face family, one for the whole film.

position.description: Where the caption block sits: lower-third, center or upper-third.

weight.description: One weight for the whole film.

continuityRules.description: The rules a reviewer can check: e.g. 'every shot is fill, never letterboxed', 'the accent appears once per section', 'no two consecutive shots share a camera height'. At least one.

footage.description: How every picture is treated, so stock, A-roll and generated stills sit in one frame.

continuity.description: The continuity rule for the footage: camera height, movement, colour temperature and shot-size progression.

orientation.description: The frame the footage is shot for; must agree with the plan aspect.

treatment.description: fill = cover and crop; blurPlate = a deliberate blurred plate behind a fitted subject.

grade.description: The one grade filter the whole film wears; it must equal the plan's grade.filter.

motion.description: The one motion language: how things enter, how they ease, how hard they push. Comps and captions may vary the idea, never the hand.

easing.description: The curve family the whole film uses for entrances and exits.

intensity.description: How far the motion pushes, 0-1; the film keeps one register.

language.description: One sentence: what motion means in this film (measured push-ins, paper cuts, kinetic type, 3D camera).

name.description: A name for the look, short enough to say on set.

palette.description: The film's palette as #rrggbb values, in order of dominance. Every generated graphic, caption accent and grade tint draws from it.

sound.description: The one sound world: the bed's duck depth and the texture that sits under the voice.

duckDb.description: The bed's duck depth; must equal audio.bgm.duckDb when a bed is present.

texture.description: One sentence: the room, the air, the low end, the transition sound.

text.description: The one text system: tokens fixed here, zones in prompts/text_animation.md.

accent.description: #rrggbb - ONE accent per video: active caption words, chapter bars, stat numbers.

ink.description: #rrggbb - white over dark/busy footage, near-black over bright.

title: FUNCUT edit plan
